title: Pass a wait flag to GUI editors in --inline mode
head: 6f72dd213141
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The new GNOME Text Editor case asserts a wait flag was logged, not that an inline edit actually waits
leads.consequence: When the editor has an already-running GUI instance, its command-line handler can hand off the file and return without waiting for that file to close. The new test passes even if --inline returns immediately in that case; its 'still waits' success line should not be treated as proof of the inline contract. This is a test-validity concern, not a request to restore the unsupported --wait flag.

leads.summary: Open PR #13044 changes the same launcher branch and restores the GNOME Text Editor --wait bug if chosen in conflict resolution
leads.consequence: The patches to the GUI *) branch cannot be applied without resolving their overlapping hunks. If #13044's case arm wins, inline gnome-text-editor receives an unsupported --wait and the current head's new GNOME case fails; if #13094's arm wins, #13044's redundant wait mapping has already been covered. Resolve the overlap explicitly, retaining the exclusion of gnome-text-editor.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator gh api (intake/related/pr-13044-files.json, patch line 9)

leads.summary: Open PR #12807 adds the same test filename and a branch that bypasses inline wait handling
leads.consequence: These two PRs both add test/shell.d/launch-editor-test.sh, an add/add file conflict. If the #12807 test is retained verbatim, its non-inline 'code' assertion fails against #13094's existing `--` operand separator. If the #12807 emacs arm is merged verbatim, it launches `setsid uwsm-app -- emacsclient ...` without -w for --inline, bypassing this PR's GUI wait behavior for Emacs. Keep both sets of tests and reconcile the emacs branch/mode on merge, rather than simply picking one new test file.
leads.triage: factual, partly wrong; add/add path conflict confirmed (intake/related/pr-12807-files.json). The no-'--' expectation conflicts with base too (base line 35 already passes --), so attribution to this PR is wrong; emacs arm is #12807's design, not this PR's defect

limits: No PR test, GUI editor, or uwsm service was executed; all findings concern source-observable test assertions and integration conflicts, not an end-to-end measurement of GUI closing behavior.

The GNOME Text Editor upstream file checked is current main at 65c089a1b75c, not a particular installed package release. This is sufficient to inspect the test's proof gap; it does not establish the runtime behavior of every release.
No package recipe, sysusers file, device identifier or group creation is added by this PR; group/device collision checks were inapplicable.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up on 6f72dd21, reassessing the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13094#issuecomment-5825874516) after the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13094#issuecomment-5833495023).

| Earlier item | Status at 6f72dd21 |
|---|---|
| `gnome-text-editor` does not accept `--wait` | Resolved |
| Directory-opening `$EDITOR` callers now wait | Still present, kept by the author by design; a maintainer decision |
| Optional `uwsm-app -t scope` | Still applies |
| Documentation note on test coverage | Still applies, plus one more stale line |

**Verified:** the VS Code inline wait from the earlier review is unchanged, and no regression was found in the changed or shared code.

### Resolved: `gnome-text-editor` no longer gets `--wait`

**Verified** with stub editors in an isolated sandbox:

```text
default editor = gnome-text-editor, --inline
3a9f5870: setsid -w uwsm-app -- gnome-text-editor --wait -- <file>   (rejected per GNOME Text Editor source)
6f72dd21: setsid -w uwsm-app -- gnome-text-editor -- <file>          (same editor argv as the base branch)
```

- Across 25 editor names and absolute paths (plus a missing-editor fallback), in inline and non-inline mode, the commit changes only the inline launch of `gnome-text-editor`. `gedit` keeps `--wait`, which gedit registers.
- The new test case fails on 3a9f5870 at "inline launch passes no --wait to gnome-text-editor" and passes on 6f72dd21.

**Remaining limit (unchanged from base):** GNOME Text Editor has no wait option. When an instance is already open, the new process hands the file to it and exits, so the launcher returns at once and `git commit` still reads the unedited message with this editor. The new test's "still waits" message only checks that `setsid -w` is passed, and the launcher comment "the caller blocks until the file is closed" does not hold for this editor. Reach stays limited because `omarchy-default-editor` does not offer it.

### Still present: directory-opening callers wait (kept by design)

The plugin-clone `--edit` terminal and the `tdl` / `hdl` editor pane are unchanged and still wait for the project window with VS Code or Zed. The author's reading that this is the `--inline` contract fits how these callers already behave: with the default TUI editor (nvim), the pane and the clone terminal already hold the editor until it exits. In the `tdl` / `hdl` pane, Ctrl-C ends only the waiting `setsid` parent and the editor keeps running (source plus a sandbox model with a stub editor). Whether these callers should get a non-waiting GUI launch is a maintainer decision.

### PR description

- The first bullet still lists `gnome-text-editor` among the editors that get `--wait`.
- It still says the test covers TUI, known GUI and unknown GUI editors in both inline and non-inline modes. Only `code` has a non-inline case.

**Suggested change:** Drop `gnome-text-editor` from that bullet, narrow the test-coverage sentence, and mention that directory-opening `$EDITOR` callers now wait for GUI editors.

**Optional, still applies:** Passing `-t scope` to `uwsm-app` in the inline branch keeps the wait independent of `UWSM_APP_UNIT_TYPE=service` in the uwsm app daemon environment, which Omarchy does not set today.

**Related open PRs:** #13044 is another fix for #13037 and still gives `gnome-text-editor` `--wait`. #12807 adds a different file at the same path, `test/shell.d/launch-editor-test.sh`.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the new commit, the launcher, the test and Omarchy's `$EDITOR` callers, plus upstream source of GNOME Text Editor (44.0 through 51.0 and `main`), GLib option parsing, gedit, util-linux `setsid`, uwsm 0.26.7 and 0.27.0, VS Code and Zed. The PR test on base, 3a9f5870 and 6f72dd21, an argv matrix and process-group experiments with the real `setsid` ran in an isolated sandbox with stub editors and a stub `uwsm-app`. No real GUI editor, uwsm daemon or desktop session was run, so editor behavior comes from source.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
